text:
New Delhi AQI Update (7th October) 

Post monsoon withdrawal AQI had spiked up however still trending better compared to last 4 years (First 6 days of October) due to better meteorological conditions and fire season yet to pick up. 
Over the weekend and next week, wind pattern will remain erratic and a few days will have easterly / SW winds along with possibility of one or two passing spell of rain in next 10 days. AQI will maintain current level with scope of getting slightly better at times. 
Post 16th October, forecasting the first proper inflection of AQI and around Dusshera avg AQI is expected to cross ~ 200 (Poor category) for the first time in this season. 
Prepare for whats ahead! 
#AQI #AirPollution

author: mssirsa
author_bio: Minister of Industries, Environment, Food & Supplies, Forest & wildlife, Government of Delhi- NCT  | Proud Indian Sikh
text:
Delhi’s air is showing a better trend, but the work is far from over.

Delhi recorded its lowest September average AQI in the last five years at 102, compared with 105 in 2025 and 108 in 2023. From January to September, Delhi also saw 194 days with AQI below 200, the highest in five years, while “Poor to Severe+” days fell to 79, the lowest in the same period.

Average PM2.5 stood at 69 µg/m³, joint lowest since 2022.

Under the leadership of Hon’ble CM Smt. @gupta_rekha Ji, we are treating pollution as a year round challenge, not a seasonal headline. From the very beginning, the focus has been on continuous monitoring, enforcement and action on the ground.

For years, while Delhi choked under toxic smog, Kejriwal and the AAP government were entirely busy polishing their own public images, blowing crores of public money on massive advertisements and building a luxurious 'Sheesh Mahal'. Combating pollution was never on their agenda.

Delhi Government is working round the clock with all concerned agencies to tackle pollution at every level. The focus is clear, action on the ground, cleaner air and a healthier Delhi for our children.
